Yesterday I had a quasi civil war with /u/SpaceRosa - as well as those that threw their jabs yesterday - over the fact that sometimes users don't post serious replies to OP's questions. Also we talked about the current flow and where it's taking this voat in which we are all on board of.

So after reflecting over many gin tonics, I concluded: Why is the [SERIOUS] not used more often? Should it be implemented as normal practice? What do you guys think? Will it actually make a difference as to the way people reply or not?
A [SERIOUS] tag will make a difference in the way most people respond, as well as the way they vote. I'm all for it.

Can we have [Serious] tags for responses instead?

Requiring [Serious] on posts will give moderators an eventual excuse for deleting responses for violating a [Serious] rule. Voat is where the goats roam free, we should preserve this by not giving away our permission to be silly.

Non Serious answers can always be downvoated and ignored. OP can gild serious answers when such a feature becomes available, to support voat and to thank users for their time and effort in coming up with a serious answer.

[Serious] tags on the post is reddit's way of doing things, see how that went.

I agree for this sub. There have been a lot of threads here in askvoat that get entirely derailed by people throwing out the quick joke for easy points. I like jokes as much as the next guy, but sometimes an interesting question is being asked, and I just want to have a discussion about the actual answer.
Is this what down voating is for? A comment that's irrelevant or rude should be just downvoated, right? I agree I like jokes. But on reddit I hate how shit gets hijacked NONSTOP. fuck

I agree with that. When we add a [Serious] tag it creates an implicit [Fuck All] tag. Anything that does not have a [Serious] tag is seen as a 'Make a super cool joke' thread. It ends up destroying the fluidity of Voat, and makes everything seem kind'a forced. While also limiting the chance of constructive conversations brought on by randomness of users' responses.
Yeah, I don't mind goofy replies, but some that are more focused maybe should have a [SERIOUS] tag

Perhaps we should at least read the rules of this subreddit and be consistent in following those rulesbefore venturing into tagging territory.

Do not spam or make clickbait posts.

As much as I agree I think people are forgetting they can collapse a branch of comments. If I care about the serious discussion and the top comment is a pun I just collapse it and it no longer feels like it's derailed. Otherwise we're just making up rules for submissions that people may not know about or follow. Plus I think having a policy of donvoating puns/jokes hides it from those who might appreciate it. My different moods affect what types of comments I want to see, so I'd rather have the ability to filter it out at that time. I think we should upvoat what speaks to us, serious or not, and leave discrimination to the reader.

I do think putting the actual serious tag on the post can be valuable to remind people you want serious answers, but I don't think pitchforks should come out for seeing an opportunity for a laugh and taking it.

Commenting on my comment because it's unrelated, I think it's great that I'm starting to recognize users from discussions I'm seeing without them being obvious karma whores. Really helps the feeling of a community.

Are you saying that we should use [Serious] in our titles, or that the site should code something similar to the [NSFW] tag to be used?

I don't think this needs to be hard-coded in. You could easily just add [Serious] to the end of your title. Mods could implement a tag in CSS if they'd like, but I think having the admins work to code something into the system should require it being something that couldn't be done without that code.

If you're saying that we as users should add it to the ends of our titles, then I'm for it. But this is up to the user posting the thread, and I don't think it should be added as standard practice. As much as I love a good Q/A thread it'll be no fun if every thread is default an "all business" thread. Leave it up to the user posting the thread, and if they use it I think it'll make a difference. What that difference is will have to be determined by what the rules are when posting in a thread tagged as [Serious]. If this is something you want to do, you may want to clearly define what these rules are in advance so people aren't confused and there isn't an issue with comments being deleted after the fact.

This is VOAT not Reddit although a great suggestion we should not be a mirror of Reddit. Perhaps you can make a subverse of Serious discussions too? I was suggested to make a RedditAnonymous subverse for those dissatisfied about how Reddit handles freedom of speech. I think in a engaging yet civil discussions after zero common ground is met gets heated then discussions should stop with the party involved. Also pm a moderator if things are getting out of hand, and your thread gets hijacked. One thing Reddit never did was taming of the trolls. We need VOAT to be unique not a Reddit parody or clone, although, I do enjoy the look of VOAT being user friendly.
